query: planning on taking it through to a finished version, for the pack I want to release, or abandoning it midway and carrying one part over — of those two, which should I be putting first?

finished a small thing in an afternoon. fine, done.
counted how many of these I actually own.
did a slow warm-up and nothing else.
the moment I commit to finishing something I stop trying things. everything after that point is executing the plan I made in the first week.
tidying, mostly. the shape's fixed by then.
recorded it on my phone to hear it back.
ordered a part and forgot what it was for.
did half an hour standing up for no reason.
compared two versions for far too long.
abandoned something in week one before it was anything.
tuned everything and then went to bed.
showed someone the thing I'm proud of. they nodded.
everything of mine that anyone has ever reacted to came out of something I abandoned and took a piece from. the finished ones are competent and nobody has ever mentioned one.
not once, and there are a lot of them.
did it while something was on in the background.
put a new string on and broke it immediately.
spent longer choosing what to work on than working.
wrote the date on a thing so I'd remember when.
restrung it and immediately put it down again.

the list existed. that's as far as it got.
